# Open Translation Questions

These items are provisional. Do not treat a suggested interpretation as
approved terminology. Review this list together with the complete `base`,
`affix`, and `default` drafts.

## Build and Distribution Gate (Not a Linguistic Review)

The current working CSVs are copied from `ja_jp` and now live in
`work/ja_jp/`; this identifies the template source, not the shipping locale.
The Korean comparison PAK keeps `en_us` filenames and its instructions select
English, but the user wants to preserve English if feasible. Confirm the
shipping locale before building. A 2026-10-06 comparison of row keys found:

- `base`: all 4,844 work `(ID_Linha, Tipo_Variante)` rows match `en_us`;
  2,241 variant values differ from `ru_ru`.
- `default`: all 65,135 work IDs match both `en_us` and `ru_ru`.
- `affix`: the work file has 3,311 Japanese-template rows; `en_us` has 586
  rows, one `FF` variant per ID, and `ru_ru` has 3,449 rows. The work key set
  matches neither target. Do not repack it for either slot unchanged.
- `zh_cn`: work `base` and `default` keys/order match exactly. All 3,311 work
  `affix` keys occur in Chinese in the same relative order, with 140
  additional Chinese rows. Resolve these before using that destination.

If `en_us` remains the target, decide and validate how the Japanese-derived
`affix` variants are reconciled to the single `FF` row for each English ID.
Do not drop variants or choose a single form silently. The equal
`estrutura_hashes*.bin` sidecars do not resolve this mismatch.

The Korean comparison PAK also adds `locatexts_en_us.characterset`, which
the inspected original lacks. Its copy under `src/lang/` is byte-identical
to the Korean comparison file, but its format, purpose, and generation
method are unknown. Preserve it exactly and include it in the full PAK build
list if following the observed Korean patch delta.

The 34-file delta was compared against one original PAK only. Confirm the
target game version, validate the rebuilt PAK by re-extraction, and perform
in-game checks before claiming compatibility. These are build/release gates,
not translation findings, and should remain separate from linguistic review.

## Audit Integrity

While reconciling the default translation map with the working CSV, quote
corruption was found and repaired for IDs 196, 368, and 410. Nineteen other
map entries still encode quotation marks as `\"`; map and CSV currently agree,
but verify whether those backslashes are intended or are serialization escapes
before any global normalization or repack.

Some existing `default` audit rows have IDs that do not match the English
source. For example, source ID 703 is `From Fomorous Hugues' Lab`, while the
audit currently labels ID 703 as `Pteryx Armor` (that string is at ID 5049).
Source ID 711 is dialogue about killing a scheming woman, while its audit row
labels it `The Chantry`. Treat existing IDs and suggested drafts as provisional
until every row is rechecked against the English CSV during the consolidated
audit review. Do not apply these notes directly to the translation CSV.

Three more source-key mismatches were confirmed while translating `default`
IDs 4700-4799: the audit labels ID 4769 `Til's Collection VIII`, but the
English source is `The chrysalae. Plant the chrysalae seeds.`; it labels ID
4770 `Glass of Ambient`, but that source is a Fateweaver/character-reset
instruction (a `Glass of Ambient` occurrence is ID 4613); and it labels ID
4794 `Master Venomguard`, but the English source is `Equip Spell 4`. Leave
these existing audit rows provisional for the consolidated audit pass.

Two further source-key mismatches were confirmed while translating `default`
IDs 4800-4899: the audit labels ID 4815 `Pickupable Item PARENT`, but the
English source is `We leveled the village... killed anyone who didn't submit.`;
it labels ID 4824 `Love Again Another Day`, but the English source is
`Wonderful. Here is the vial.`. Leave the old audit rows untouched until the
consolidated audit pass, and verify their actual source IDs then.
